# sec-filing-ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 in a uv workspace of four packages (from the repository scaffold).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/s (SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks of downloading for the full history at 3 requests/s (index row count times request rate; not yet measured) |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until the submissions are on disk (no basis yet) |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression). One track: each outcome consumes the one before it.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table
      Objective: Load the real quarterly and daily index files into one filing-index table, run once by hand.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a filing-index table over the quarterly history and the current quarter's daily files; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the table holds one row per index entry from the real quarterly and daily files, with the row count per file reported; the findings file records the real run's elapsed time, request count and data volume
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the submissions that the filing-index table names.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table and findings file
      Produces: submission files on disk for the downloaded range, with a list of rows whose download failed
      Exit: O2 — every index row in the downloaded range has its submission on disk or appears in the failure list, and the measured download rate is recorded
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submission files and Stage 1's table
      Produces: extracted main documents for the 10-K and 8-K filings in the downloaded range
      Exit: O3 — each 10-K and 8-K submission in the range has its main document extracted or is listed with the reason it was not
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and traceability
      Objective: Make every table row, submission and extracted document traceable to the stored source bytes it came from, and replayable from them.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 outputs
      Produces: a manifest of ingested sources with content hashes; replay from stored bytes
      Exit: O1–O3 — each row and document names its source file and hash, and a rebuild from stored bytes reproduces the outputs with no SEC requests
      Leaves out: point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time awareness
      Objective: Record later changes to quarterly indexes as dated changes rather than overwrites.
      Outcomes: O1 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifest and stored source bytes
      Produces: a filing-index table readable as of a past date, with recorded additions, changes and withdrawals
      Exit: O1 — re-reading a changed quarterly index records each difference with its date and source, and the table read as of an earlier date returns the earlier rows
      Leaves out: full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suites
      Objective: Cover the index, download and extraction paths with tests on committed fixtures.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stages 1–5 outputs
      Produces: a CI suite that downloads nothing from the SEC
      Exit: O1–O3 — CI passes on fixtures for each index format in the ingested range, for failed and partial downloads, and for 10-K and 8-K extraction, and malformed inputs fail closed
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run daily index ingestion and the downstream steps unattended on a deployed platform.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stages 1–6 outputs
      Produces: deployed, scheduled ingestion with catch-up after missed runs
      Exit: O1–O3 — observed scheduled runs ingest each new daily index and its submissions, and a missed day is caught up on the next run
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
